A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHuBERT with the same authors and core research framework. The complete main texts, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation, isolated sign recognition, phonological feature recognition and ablation results, supplemented by cluster visualizations and translation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds fingerspelling detection, original-WLASL2000 evaluation and input-stream ablation results.

M1.justification: Core SHuBERT pre-training remains unchanged: four input streams, per-stream clustering, masking and cross-entropy prediction. The described downstream adaptations narrow: v2 retains rank-1 LoRA for ISLR but drops v1's joint multi-dataset procedure with a shared encoder, separate classification heads and equally weighted losses.

E1.justification: v2 adds ASL-Stem-Wiki fingerspelling detection, extending evaluation to temporal localization of fingerspelling segments (Section 4.4). Existing translation, ISLR and phonological recognition coverage remains; phonological experiments move to Appendix B. The cleaned-to-original WLASL change concerns the evaluation setting within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds VAP and Uni-Sign to the How2Sign and OpenASL comparisons. Its WLASL comparison replaces SVT, BEVT, VideoMAE and MaskFeat with SignBERT, SignBERT+, MSLU, NLA-SLR and Uni-Sign. The new fingerspelling experiment compares against Yin et al.'s contrastive-learning method. SignMusketeers becoming SM is only a renamed table entry.

E3.justification: WLASL evaluation changes from the cleaned version with Recall@1/5/10 to the original version with per-instance and per-class top-1 accuracy. New protocols include cross-validation with IoU for fingerspelling detection and a How2Sign stream experiment feeding features directly to T5 without pre-training. These changes preclude treating the WLASL scores as same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: v2 removes the comparison of LoRA, full fine-tuning and joint training across three ISLR datasets, eliminating evidence about adaptation strategy and joint-training benefits. It adds an input-stream contribution experiment in Appendix A, Table 8. Existing masking, data-scale, layer-combination and freezing ablations are retained, as are the cluster analyses and translation examples.

E5.justification: The new fingerspelling experiment explicitly introduces cross-validation, a resampling-based performance estimation procedure. However, v2 supplies no fold count or uncertainty estimates. Neither version reports random-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: New results include fingerspelling mean IoU of 0.40 versus 0.28, stream-ablation scores, and original-WLASL accuracies of 60.90 per-instance and 58.01 per-class. Full and joint ISLR result rows are omitted. Translation scores, retained ASL Citizen/Sem-Lex LoRA scores and phonological accuracies are unchanged. Adding VAP reduces the reported OpenASL advantage from 10.0 to 2.0 BLEU without changing SHuBERT's score.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.4 adds a formal input/output definition of fingerspelling detection using an ordered frame sequence and a set of start/end-frame intervals. There are no new theorems or proofs. Additional feature and cluster notation in Section 3 explains the unchanged learning objective.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a contextual, multi-stream self-supervised representation transferable across sign-language tasks. v2 expands the abstract and introduction's explicit performance claims to fingerspelling detection, while replacing v1's detailed numerical headline improvements with broader task-level claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explicit limitation that potential biases have not been systematically studied despite encouraging cluster visualizations. It also explains MSASL exclusion and qualifies Uni-Sign's OpenASL comparison through pre-training/test overlap. Earlier limitations concerning absolute performance, scaling and generalization beyond ASL remain.

D1.justification: v2 states that the model is publicly available and supplies a project address, replacing v1's promised release. It adds a SacreBLEU signature, the 100-video manual check underlying hand-detection accuracy, and parameter counts. Conversely, removed full-fine-tuning details leave Appendix B referring to a procedure no longer described in Section 4.3.

R1.justification: v2 incorporates relevant newer comparisons, including VAP and Uni-Sign, and sharpens its distinction from SignBERT+ through discussion of RGB fusion and pre-training data exposure. It trims generic text/speech background and adds an ASL-focused data rationale. The central positioning around contextual, joint multi-stream self-supervision is retained; SignMusketeers and C2RL publication updates do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Phonological recognition and detailed ablations move from the main text into Appendices B and A, fingerspelling detection becomes a main experimental section, and the former supplementary sections become Appendices C–E. Method explanations and experimental narration are also substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: Three translation tables become one cross-dataset table, and three ISLR tables become another consolidated table with parameter counts and revised metrics. Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, existing tables and cluster figures are relocated or reordered, and new detection and stream-ablation tables appear. Figure 1 retains older ISLR comparisons without reconciling them with the revised Table 2.

improvement.justification: The new temporal detection experiment broadens evidence for transfer, while updated baselines and explicit overlap qualifications make the comparisons more informative. Stream analysis and clearer access information add useful support. These gains are limited by removal of the ISLR adaptation study, Appendix B's incomplete training reference, and Figure 1's unreconciled older comparisons. The net improvement is modest, with the main translation results unchanged.
